40: /**
41:  * Handles the {@code @UtilityClass} annotation for javac.

46: 	@Override public void handle(AnnotationValues<UtilityClass> annotation, JCAnnotation ast, JavacNode annotationNode) {
47: 		handleExperimentalFlagUsage(annotationNode, ConfigurationKeys.UTILITY_CLASS_FLAG_USAGE, "@UtilityClass");
48:

50: 		
51: 		JavacNode typeNode = annotationNode.up();
52: 		if (!checkLegality(typeNode, annotationNode)) return;
53: 		typeNode.getAst().changeModifiersAndGenerateConstructor(typeNode);

56: 	private static boolean checkLegality(JavacNode typeNode, JavacNode errorNode) {
57: 		if (!isClass(typeNode)) {
58: 			errorNode.addError("@UtilityClass is only supported on a class.");
59: 			return false;
60: 		}
61: 		
62: 		// It might be an inner class. This is okay, but only if it is / can be a static inner class. Thus, all of its parents have to be static inner classes until the top-level.
63: 		JavacNode typeWalk = typeNode;
64: 		while (true) {
65: 			typeWalk = typeWalk.up();
66: 			switch (typeWalk.getKind()) {
67: 			case TYPE:
68: 				JCClassDecl typeDef = (JCClassDecl) typeWalk.get();
69: 				if ((typeDef.mods.flags & (Flags.STATIC | Flags.ANNOTATION | Flags.ENUM | Flags.INTERFACE)) != 0) continue;

part.text: The conventional static-nesting rewrite is incompatible with javac’s generic-method inference, while omitting it breaks legacy nested instantiation. I’ll retain it only for utility classes without generic methods, where it is required; generic utility classes use javac’s normal enclosing type and still receive static AST modifiers.

The rewrite is now gated only when a utility class declares generic methods, matching the precise failure condition while retaining legacy symbol handling otherwise. I’ll run the full benchmark target and inspect the final diff.
